## 2026-09-18T06:30:08Z — gate R1′ part 2r — the ladder from the frontier under the simple system — commit `d9b2ca177` (tree DIRTY) — 0/12 green

Reading this section: every row is a CHAIN of legs bounded by TICKS (never by the wall), resumed from the previous leg's --stop-snapshot, so a leg boundary is reproducible (§12b.2 item 11) and "twice equal" measures the table, not the box. "NEW marks" lists only marks that do NOT already hold at the frontier (M01–M10 hold there, and so does M13 under R1′'s sharpened predicate — the measurement is in ladder/ptr.json). A row with NEW marks: NONE is a WALL, not a failure: the curve beside it is the deliverable (what was accumulating, at what rate, and what stopped moving). An instantaneous `points` reading is NOT comparable between configurations — it is sampled wherever the p reset cycle happened to be (§12b.2 item 15); compare the structural quantities (TC, Time Energy and its cap, EP, SE, Generator Power, boosters, upgrades held, unlockOrder). ticks_ms and the 1-minute load are on every long row: this battery ran with 8 CPU-bound children on 8 cores, so ms/tick is roughly double the quiet-box 19–25 ms — that moves wall time, never game-seconds.

## 2026-09-18T14:37:48Z — gate M1, the mobile layout AND the nav bar (`node tools/harness/page.mjs --gate mobile`) — commit `eeef20332` (tree DIRTY: this slice's own changes, committed straight after the run) — 171/171 green

Viewport 390x844, touch emulated, `?mobile=1`. Legs per game: inertness (neither flag) · state (200x0.05 plain, a plain CONTROL, then mobile) · geometry (fresh tree + every tab the deepest snapshot opens) · nav bar · `?mobile=1&automation=1` where the game has a table · **navbar-only at 1280x800 with no touch, against the plain desktop page as the control** · load (same `manifest.load.known` allowances as G1).

The navbar-only leg is new in this slice (`?navbar=1`, the bar without the layout). It runs in a SECOND context at
1280x800 with **no touch**, and measures the navbar-only page against the **plain desktop page, view for view** —
`#treeOverlay` position, `#app` column-count and `.col` widths all equal the plain page's (plus the absolute
reading: a `.col` is 35-65% of the viewport), nothing escapes sideways that the plain page does not, and the plain
page is asserted inert (which is the inertness leg over again at a second viewport, free). Three mutants at `ptr`,
each RED, each restored: `mobile.css` linked under `?navbar=1` (caught by the stylesheet check alone; the rules are
scoped, so no geometry moved), the `tmt-mobile` CLASS **and** the sheet (caught by geometry: `.col` 634 -> 1280,
`#treeOverlay` `absolute` -> `relative`/`static`, one control escaping where the control page had none), and
`navbar.js` guarded on `mobile` again (no bar, `navH` 0).

Also measured for this slice, on `ptr` at 1280x800: a fixed bar over a page whose layout is NOT page-scrolling hid
the bottom of every scrolled tab — lowest control bottom 796 px under a bar whose top is at 743. `navbar.css`
shortens `.col` / `.fullWidth` by `--tmt-navbar-h` (with `min-height: 0`, without which the engines' own
`min-height: 100%` wins and nothing moves) -> 739 px, column width unchanged at 634 px.

## 2026-09-18T20:08:07Z — gate M1, the mobile layout, the nav bar AND the layer list (`node tools/harness/page.mjs --gate mobile`) — commit `5f3c04403` (tree DIRTY: this slice's own changes, committed straight after the run) — 170/171 green


Viewport 390x844, touch emulated, `?mobile=1`. Legs per game: inertness (neither flag) · state (200x0.05 plain, a plain CONTROL, then mobile) · geometry (fresh tree + every tab the deepest snapshot opens) · nav bar · `?mobile=1&automation=1` where the game has a table · navbar-only at 1280x800 with no touch, against the plain desktop page as the control · **the LAYER LIST, at both widths** · load (same `manifest.load.known` allowances as G1).

The layers leg is new in this slice (U2). At each width it asserts: the Layers button exists and is immediately
left of Tree; one card per shown layer as a SET against the engine's own answer (`tmp[l].layerShown`, truthy and
not `'ghost'`, for a layer with a row), computed in the probe and not asked of the list; every card in the section
its `tmp[l].row` names; distinct chips on each card; and the geometry — zero escaping controls and zero under 44 px
on the phone, and against the plain desktop page IN THE SAME STATE at 1280 px (the engines' own `.back` is 38x50
there on the plain page too). Then two things a rendering test cannot fake: the state hash is UNCHANGED across
opening the list (with the leg's own control — two hashes back to back — and an abstention where the page will not
repeat its own hash), and the card's reset button MOVES `player[l].points` when pressed on a layer that both
`canReset` and has a `resetGain` above 0.

Seven mutants, each RED, each restored, each on the game that can see it: the Layers button right of Tree
(`buttonLeftOfTree`, ptr); the card set taken from `player[l].unlocked` too (13 cards vs the engine's 11, ptr); the
chips' digit phase removed, leaving the token extension alone (duplicate chips, the-mechanic-tree AND
falling-mountain-s-alterprestige); the reset button wired to nothing (NOT MOVED, ptr); chips at a 30 px minimum
(tooSmall, ptr); the engine's NaN flag left raised (layersInert MOVED, the-quantum-tree); and `updateTemp()` driven
from the list again (layersInert MOVED, the-periodic-table-tree). FOUR of the seven are GREEN on ptr — a battery run
only on the reference game would have called this leg proven while blind to every defect it in fact found.

Also measured for this slice, and fixed: a game's own `* { margin: auto; text-align: center }` reaches into the
overlay (ptr) and shrink-wrapped the list body to 447 px inside a 1280 px panel; `player.hasNaN` is raised by the
engines' own `format()` when a game's prestige text formats a NaN (the-quantum-tree's `Qc`); `updateTemp()` writes
`player` on the-periodic-table-tree (`He.Inflate` 3 -> 4); `canReset` does not imply a gain in TMT 2.7
(the-chronicle-tree); an id handed to `buyUpgrade` must be a NUMBER (`["11"]` vs `[11]`); a click is not a neutral
probe (the-dressy-tree counts every click on the document); and a disambiguating digit must be checked against the
WHOLE chip set rather than incremented, since a base can itself end in a digit ("N"+28 == "N2"+8, measured on
falling-mountain-s-alterprestige's 58-component `Nanoprestige`).

⚠ The one RED is `the-periodic-table-tree`, and its LAYERS leg is entirely green — it is the STATE leg, on one of
the games the roster already knows does not repeat its own hash. That leg abstains when its plain CONTROL differs;
here the two plain runs agreed by chance and the mobile one did not, so it reported MOVED instead of abstaining.
MEASURED: three solo runs of that game right after this sweep, all GREEN, all abstaining. **The state leg's control
is a single repeat, so a game with three distinct hashes can pass the control by luck and then red on the mobile
leg — the abstention is not reliable.** That is pre-existing (it is U1's leg) and is written down here for whoever
hardens it; nothing in this slice touches the state leg.

## 2026-09-18T22:35:04Z — gate M1, the mobile layout, the nav bar AND the layer list whose chips MIRROR THE NORMAL VIEW (`node tools/harness/page.mjs --gate mobile`) — commit `e3ba99c74` (tree DIRTY: this slice's own changes, committed straight after the run) — 171/171 green

U2b: the layer list's chips now MIRROR THE GAME'S OWN TAB — ⚖ four user requests (2026-09-18) answered by one
walker over each layer's `tabFormat`: chips only for what the tab draws, in the order it draws them, with a
divider at every category change and milestones given chips of their own with SQUARE corners. U2's state ordering
is gone; state is a chip's appearance, never its position.

Reading the new columns in the notes:
· **chip sequence = tabFormat order** — the DOM sequence against an expectation rebuilt inside the probe out of
  `tmp[l].tabFormat`, with the same three visibility rules. Never asked of the list: a list compared against its
  own `chipsOf` would assert nothing.
· **dividers** — measured on what the browser RENDERS, in BOTH states (collapsed and expanded), by reading each
  element's computed `display`. This closes U2's named gap, "the leg never presses a card's `+N` button".
· **milestone radius vs the rest** — square against round, where the page has both kinds.
· **off source order** — cards whose sequence differs from U2's (every upgrade, then buyable, then challenge, by
  id). This is the DISCRIMINATOR for the sort: a sort that changes nothing is untested.
· **U2b discriminators** (the two reference games only, against `U2_CHIPS` in `page.mjs`) — the chip count must
  have FALLEN against U2's recorded 120 / 70, and it must fall even though U2b ADDS the milestones.
· **U2b rules** — visibility rule 2 (`pseudoUnl`) and the milestones' second condition (`milestoneShown`, which
  reads the player's `msDisplay`) are exercised by NO recorded snapshot state on the roster, so the leg constructs
  each condition on the phone page after the reset press, re-runs the independent expectation under it, and
  restores. A game that cannot see one abstains, naming itself.
· **cards hiding a whole category behind `+N`** — REPORTED, asserted by nothing. The collapsed card's selection
  rule is still U2's flat "first six"; ⚖ the user has redesigned that card outright, so U2b is the EXPANDED view.

State leg: **165 equal, 0 moved, 6 abstained** (the-periodic-table-tree, the-cookie-tree,
falling-mountain-s-alterprestige, the-gaming-tree, plague-tree-vorona-cirus-treesease, the-orchard-tree) — the
first of those was U2's one RED, and it abstains here because it runs at or after `e3ba99c74`, the state leg's
adaptive-confirmation fix. Navbar-only leg: 171/171 green over 173 views.

Layers leg: **171/171 green over 974 cards and 1092 chips**, at 390px with touch and at 1280px without. Opening the
list moved no state hash in 171/171. Reset press: 146 moved `player[l].points`, 0 did not, 25 abstained — the same
counts U2 recorded, which is the claim that nothing about the chips changed what the cards DO.

**U2b's own numbers.** 974 cards carry **1092 chips**, against U2's **3222** over the same 974 cards: the
visibility rules remove about two thirds of what U2 showed, and they do it while ADDING 216 milestone chips. 53
dividers. `tabFormat` over the SHOWN layers: **420 array-form, 271 object/subtab-form, 283 declaring none** (the
engine default). **85 of the 276 chip-bearing cards are NOT in source order.** The two reference games against
their recorded baselines: `ptr` **120 → 83** (24 milestones, 6 of 7 cards off source order), `something`
**70 → 30** (5 milestones, 1 of 3).

**The two constructed visibility rules.** `msDisplay='never'` hid every milestone chip on the **55** games that
have one and abstained on the other 116; `pseudoUnl` forced true produced pseudo chips on **4** games — exactly
the four whose engine defines the global (`ptr`, `prestige-tree-ng`, `prestige-tree-rewritten-unsoftcapped4`,
`the-extended-tree`) — and abstained on 167. Every game restored its own state. ⚠ **At their natural states the
roster draws ZERO pseudo-unlocked upgrades**, which is why the rule is constructed rather than waited for.

**The collapsed card, reported and not asserted**: 8 of the 47 multi-category cards leave a whole category behind
the `+N` (`ptr/t` and `ptr/s` hide their upgrades, `ptr/q` its buyables, `the-unbalanced-tree`'s `inf`/`e`/`r` and
`a-game-about-rocks/s` their challenges, `the-melge-tree/i` its milestones). ⚖ The user has redesigned the
collapsed card outright, so U2b is the EXPANDED view and that selection rule is still U2's.

**Eight mutants**, each RED on a game that can see it, control GREEN either side — the table is in
[docs/mobile.md](../../../docs/mobile.md). ⚠ Mutant A ("use the engine default even where a `tabFormat` exists")
is GREEN on `ptr`, `something`, `the-algebra-tree` AND `the-game-tree`; finding `the-elemental-tree` and
`the-point-tree` took a 171-game roster scan. ⚠ Mutant C hid itself under the first version of the rule probe,
which scored "the chips did not move" as an abstention.

## 2026-09-19T00:47:58Z — gate M1, the LAYER LIST's COLLAPSED CARD: a counter row over a button row (`node tools/harness/page.mjs <9 games> --gate mobile`) — commit `5434d5110` (tree DIRTY: this slice's own changes, committed straight after the run) — 9/9 green, a BOUNDED local set; CI owns the roster

U2d: ⚖ the COLLAPSED card is now **two rows** (user, 2026-09-18) — a COUNTER per category the layer's own tab
draws, and under it an ACTION BUTTON per component that is unlocked and not yet bought. U2's flat "first six
chips, then `+N`" is gone, and with it the question it raised: the tab layout puts milestones first, so the first
six could be nothing but the passive category, and U2b measured **8 of the roster's 47 multi-category cards hiding
a whole category behind the `+N`**. Those eight cards are now the leg's own DISCRIMINATORS. **The chips are the
expanded view**, untouched from U2b.

Reading the new columns in the notes:
· **counters** — one per category the tab draws, in tab-layout order: `x/y` earned over drawn for milestones,
  upgrades, challenges and achievements; ⚖ THE TOTAL OWNED, one number, for buyables and clickables (the user's
  choice over an `x/y` whose denominator would mean nothing for something that is never "done"). Milestones keep
  their SQUARE corners. Compared against an expectation rebuilt inside the probe out of `tmp` / `player`.
· **button set** — ⚖ unlocked and not yet bought, in tab-layout order, NEVER "affordable right now": affordability
  decides lit-vs-grey and nothing else. Also rebuilt in the probe, which is what catches a build that selects on
  affordability without waiting for anything to move.
· **row fit** — ⚖ as many buttons as the row holds, MEASURED at render against the row's own box, never a
  constant: the visible ones are a prefix of the offer, all on one line, and nothing sticks out past the card.
· **two rows** — no counter shares a line with a button, measured on the ELEMENTS (an empty `.…-actions` box left
  behind by a single-row build would make a container test abstain rather than fail), and judged only where the
  card has something in both. The cards that would look *wrong* under a single-row build are named at every run.
· **collapsed ≠ expanded** — a card that renders the same in both states is a card this leg cannot judge. ⚠ The
  visibility test is now `getClientRects()`, not computed `display`: the collapsed card hides the whole chip ROW,
  and a child of a `display: none` parent still reports its own computed display.
· **fit / stability / throttle / counter press** — the four legs that have to DRIVE something, each abstaining by
  name rather than passing in silence.

**The bounded local set, and why these nine.** ⚖ Since U2h the full sweep runs sharded in CI on every push, so a
slice verifies `ptr`, `something` and whatever its own change can be seen on, and reads the roster's verdict from
the `merge + roster assertion` job. Here that is the seven games carrying the cards U2b measured hiding a whole
category behind the `+N` — `ptr` (`t`, `s`, `q`), `the-unbalanced-tree` (`inf`, `e`, `r`), `a-game-about-rocks`
(`s`), `the-melge-tree` (`i`) — plus `the-elemental-tree` and `the-point-tree` (U2b's mutant-A games, the ones
whose `tabFormat` does NOT follow the engine default), `the-alphabetree` (49 cards) and `the-quantum-tree` (the
NaN-flag game).

⚠ **`ptr` abstains on two of the four driving legs** — nothing is affordable at its deep snapshot and no card
offers more buttons than its row already holds — so the fit and the counter press are proved by `something`,
`the-unbalanced-tree`, `a-game-about-rocks`, `the-alphabetree` and `the-quantum-tree`, not by the reference game.
A battery run only on `ptr` would have called both legs proven while they were vacuous.

Alongside: `node --test loader/*.test.mjs` **33/33**, `gates-s1.mjs --part 1` **52/52 green** (the read-only claim
— the list still assigns nothing to `player` and adds no clickable id), and the M1 legs that predate U2d all green
over the same nine games (inertness 9 unchanged, state 9 equal, reset press 7 moved / 2 abstained — the same two
that abstained under U2b).

**Eight mutants, each RED, each restored, control GREEN either side** (docs/mobile.md carries the table): A
affordability used for SELECTION (`something`); B the fit from a constant 6 (`the-unbalanced-tree`); C the
counters' corners swapped (`ptr`); C2 the CHIPS' corners swapped (`ptr` — **GREEN under U2b's "they differ" test**,
which is why both radius checks now assert which is which); D the counters unthrottled (`ptr`); E a buyable
counter as `x/y` (`ptr`); F the two rows collapsed into one (`the-unbalanced-tree`); G "is it an amount?" asked as
`isFinite(toNumber())` (`ptr`).

⚠ **Two of the eight were first written WRONG and would have been recorded as passes.** A's temporal leg
ABSTAINED on its own defect — a build that selects on affordability starts with an empty row, so its lit/grey
vector never moves, and the leg skipped any card that had no buttons before the ticks. F's first construction
moved the actions box inside the counters box at build time, i.e. before `drawCounters` cleared that box, so the
buttons ended up detached and the card rendered none at all: a red on the set check, not on the two-row one.

⚠ **G is a defect this slice shipped and then found, after the whole bounded set was green.** "Is this value an
amount?" was asked as `isFinite(v.toNumber())`, which is FALSE for any Decimal past 1.8e308 — and a TMT save
reaches there routinely (`ptr`'s own points read 6.7e3284 at the gate's snapshot). No recorded state has a
BUYABLE up there, so all 171 games would have stayed green while a real buyable was dropped out of its own total.
The question is about the TYPE now, in both implementations, and the leg constructs the condition (one drawn
buyable given 1e400) exactly as it constructs `msDisplay` and `pseudoUnl`.

⚠ **A grid defect U2 shipped, found by this requirement.** `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(280px, 1fr))` gives a 1280px
desktop FOUR columns of **308px** against a phone's single **366px** card — the desktop card was NARROWER, so ⚖
"more buttons on a desktop" was unbuildable however the fit was measured. Now `minmax(min(100%, 380px), 1fr)`:
**366 → 413px**, three columns, and every viewport above the phone's holds a card at least as wide as the phone's.

### The first CI sweep at `daeab5795` found a defect this slice did not write — and neither did U2d's own bounded set

`171/171 covered, 1 RED: the-modding-tree`, read from the `merge + roster assertion` job (⛔ never from the shard
checkmarks: nine were green and the tenth's failure is what carried it). The verdict: `counter=NOT MOVED`,
`0/1 → 0/1` on `p/11`.

⚠ **`buyUpgrade` is an ALIAS the TMT engines grew later.** Censused over the roster: **169 of 171 games define
`buyUpgrade`, 170 define `buyUpg`, and exactly two — `the-modding-tree` (2.0.5.1) and `the-burning-tree` — define
only `buyUpg`.** So since U2 a chip press on those two called a function that does not exist and bought nothing.
It survived two slices because **no gate had ever DRIVEN a chip**: the layers leg pressed the reset button and
nothing else, and a press that silently does nothing looks exactly like a press with nothing to do. U2d's counter
press is the first leg that buys, and it is what turned the defect into a red.

⚠ **`the-burning-tree` did NOT red** — its counter press abstains, because nothing is affordable at its state. One
of the two carried the whole finding, which is the shape of the roster-owns-the-verdict argument: a bounded local
set of nine could not have contained it, and the reference games both define the alias.

Fixed by calling whichever name the engine has; both games GREEN afterwards, and the pre-fix CI run is the mutant
record for it.
